MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  August 18, 2014

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Kelley at 5:03 p.m., on August 18, 2014, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on August 13, 2014, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Reardon (arrived at 5:04 p.m.)
  Council Member Schlicht (arrived at 5:15 p.m.)
  Council Member Ury
  Mayor Pro Tem Leckness
  Mayor Kelley

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Cheryl Dyas/Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel: Anticipated Litigation Initiation of Litigation
  pursuant to subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9: 2 potential cases.

CS2. Conference with Labor Negotiators Agency Representatives: Mr. Wilberg, Ms. Dyas,
  Ms. Goetz, and City Attorney Curley. Unrepresented employee: Medical Coverage
  Issue.

City Council Minutes  1  August 18, 2014
 CS3. Conference with Legal Counsel - Anticipated Litigation: Initiation of litigation
  pursuant to subdivision (c) of Section 54956.9: 1 potential case.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:06 p.m., Mayor Kelley recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:02 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Ury

INVOCATION: Mayor Pro Tem Leckness

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that there were originally three Closed Session agenda items
however, items CS2 and CS3 were removed because the matters were no longer necessary.

For item CS1, the City Council directed staff to communicate, through the Mayor's office, with
the County Board of Supervisors and ask that the County defer action on a proposed probation
office in Mission Viejo.

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Adopted Headquarters Battalion of the 1st Marine Division Quarterly Recognition

  Mayor Kelley presented certificates of commendation to "Marine of the Quarter" Lance
  Corporal Deonte L. Lang and "Noncommissioned Officers of the Quarter" Corporal Phuong
  Tsan and Sergeant Nicholas J. Horschler.

P2. Presentation by OCSD Captain Brian Schmutz on the new Saddleback Station in Lake
  Forest

  The City Council received the presentation from OCSD Captain Brian Schmutz.

P3. Featured Business of the Month - CAllie Girl Clothing Store

  Mayor Kelley presented the proclamation to Jennifer Arnott, owner of CAllie Girl Clothing
  Store.

P4. Pros and Cons of E-Cigarettes

  The City Council received the presentation from Norm Bour, founder of Vape Mentors, Tom
  Kiklas, President and Co-founder of the Tobacco Vapor Electronic Cigarette Association,
  Mike Pixomatis, OCSD Sergeant and Drug Liaison, and Phil Falcetti, CEO of National
  Council on Alcoholism and Drug Dependence - Orange County.

City Council Minutes  2  August 18, 2014
   Marilyn MacDougall, M.V.: stated that our children are our most precious resource and she
  asked the City Council to make sure that they are protecting our children as they look at
  expanding tobacco centers/e-cig vapor stores.

RECESS

At the hour of 7:04 p.m., Mayor Kelley declared a recess. The City Council reconvened 7:14 p.m.
with all five City Council Members present.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Larry Gilbert, M.V.: expressed concern that Code Enforcement Officer Rottmann and Council
Member Reardon paid a surprise visit to South County Vapors and, in light of the public hearing
on tonight's agenda, he stated that Gestapo tactics should not be used on someone who wants to
run a legitimate business in the City.

Debbie Peel, M.V.: stated that the Special Fire Protection Area is an example of exactly what the
City should be doing for the residents. The SFPA has preserved residents’ authority over their own
property and she noted that continually bringing the matter up does nothing but stir up dissent and
confuse homeowners and HOAs.

Margot Ferron, M.V.: announced that the American Cancer Society will partner with Stand-Up to
Cancer to form a dream team to find a cure for lung cancer. Mission Viejo has been selected to
host a viewing party on September 5, 2014, from 7:00 to 9:00 p.m. at the Norman P. Murray
Community Center.

Kevin Astor, Principal of Capistrano Valley High School: provided some history and context
regarding the permit parking changes in the neighborhood adjacent to CVHS. He noted that he
misunderstood city staff's request that he push information out to the community and he expressed
that there are some concerns which should be considered during future discussions of parking near
CVHS.

Anna Warner, M.V.: discussed the home she purchased in June of 2014 which has water damage,
mold and asbestos problems. She asked why building permits were issued when the home clearly
does not meet California building standards.

Christina Lee, Capistrano Beach: as a teacher and parent at CVHS, she expressed concern with the
change in hours for parking in the neighborhood near Capistrano Valley High School. She stated
that the school community would like to work together and come to an agreement that will benefit
everyone.

Stacy Joyce, M.V.: stated that there were several key points that were not addressed when the
Council voted to place parking restrictions in the neighborhood adjacent to CVHS. She said that
the residents next to CVHS freely chose to live near a well-established high school and should not
be surprised by parking issues.

City Council Minutes  3  August 18, 2014
 Doreen McKernan, M.V.: asked the City Council to change the Coronado permit parking program
hours back to the previous time frame of 9:30 a.m. to 1:30 p.m.

Karen Wise, M.V.: expressed concern with the precedence the city is setting with neighborhoods
mobilizing to present petitions and concerns to the Council without obvious opposition from the
other side. She stated that the parking restrictions have created huge safety and traffic concerns
with only one way in and out of the CVHS campus.

Sue Dennis, M.V.: requested that the parking restrictions surrounding CVHS be returned to the
original time of 9:30 a.m. to 1:30 p.m.

Rafael Pintor, M.V.: stated that public streets should be kept public and he asked that the Coronado
Homes parking restrictions be reverted to the previous hours.

The following presented written comments in favor of reverting the parking permit hours back to
the previous time frame of 9:30 a.m. to 1:30 p.m.: Lorraine Gaul, M.V.: Si Herbers, M.V.; and
Susan Carroll, M.V.

Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: asked questions about the City of Laguna Hills police cost study, the
proposed OCFA pension obligation legislation, and the City Attorney’s opinion on whether or not
the City is liable for OCFA’s unfunded liability.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12, 17 and 21were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate
discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further
  reading waived.

10. Check Register Dated July 25, 2014 in the Amount of $855,503.28

City Council Minutes  4  August 18, 2014
   Ratified the accompanying check register.

13. City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for June 2014

  Received and filed.

14. Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Monthly Report for June 2014

  Received and filed.

15. Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for June 2014

  Received and filed.

16. Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly Report
  for June 2014

  Received and filed.

18. Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA) Master Funding Agreement

  Approved Amendment 2 to Master Funding Agreement No. C-1-2775 Between Orange
  County Transportation Authority (OCTA) and City of Mission Viejo for M2 Comprehensive
  Transportation Funding Programs.

19. La Paz Bridge/Road Widening (CIP 756/761)

  Authorized the payment of a $50,000 deposit to the Southern California Regional Rail
  Authority (SCRRA) for construction support services.

20. 2013 Residential Resurfacing-Asphalt Overlays (CIP 838)

  (1) Certified the completion of and accepted the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City Clerk
  to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the faithful
  performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days, respectively, after the date of
  recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being filed with
  the City; and (4) authorized the release of the final retention 35 days after the date of
  recordation of the Notice of Completion.

City Council Minutes  5  August 18, 2014
 22. 2014 Residential Resurfacing (CIP 838)-Slurry Seal

  Awarded the construction contract for the subject project to Roy Allan Slurry Seal, Inc., in
  the amount of $299,248.50.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

24. Appeal filed by Council Member Rhonda Reardon of the Planning and Transportation
  Commission’s Approval of Conditional Use Permit CUP2014-333, a petition submitted
  by South County Vapors Inc., to operate an electronic cigarette retail store located at
  the Mission Viejo Business Center, 23891 Via Fabricante, Suite 611, in the BP (Business
  Park/ Industrial) zone.

  Director of Community Development Elaine Lister presented the staff report.

  Mayor Kelley opened the public hearing at 8:16 p.m.

  Syliva Maxson, Applicant, South County Vapors: discussed her business, the location, and
  her diligence to not sell e-cigarettes or e-cig products to minors.

  The following spoke in support of the petition by South County Vapors, Inc. to operate an
  electronic cigarette retail store on Via Fabricante: Griffin Beltran, M.V.; Lucy Noble, Chino
  Hills; Brian Gage, Los Angeles; Gavin Tucker, Orange County; Joshua Lawler, M.V.;
  Rodger Bendinelli, M.V.; Dallas Brink, M.V.; James Lewis (no city of residence given; and
  Jay Oku, Irvine.

  Letitia Clark George, Executive Director/Community Engagement Director of the American
  Academy of Pediatrics, Orange County Chapter: expressed concern about e-cigarette stores
  taking precautions to see that the devices do not get into the hands of minors.

  Syliva Maxson, Applicant, South County Vapors: provided brief rebuttal comments in
  response to the public speakers and to the Council Member's questions.

  At the hour of 9:21 p.m., Mayor Kelley closed the public hearing.

  The Council Members made comments and asked questions of staff.

  Motion made by Council Member Reardon, seconded by Council Member Ury, to affirm the
  Planning and Transportation Commission's action and adopt Resolution 14-38 Denying the
  Appeal Petition and Approving CUP2014-333 Being a Petition Submitted by South County
  Vapors, Inc., to Operate an Electronic Cigarette Retail Store Located at the Mission Viejo
  Business Center, 23891 Via Fabricante, Suite 611, in the Business Park/Industrial Zone.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  6  August 18, 2014
   AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

RECESS

Mayor Kelley declared a recess at the hour of 9:41 p.m. The City Council reconvened at 9:48 p.m.
with all five City Council Members present.

PUBLIC HEARINGS (Continued)

23. Public Hearing to Consider All Objections to the Proposed Abatement of Weeds on
  Parcels Less than One Acre for the Annual Weed Abatement Program 2014 - Phase 2

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  Mayor Kelley opened the public hearing at 9:53 p.m. Upon hearing no requests to speak,
  Mayor Kelley closed the public hearing.

  Council Member Schlicht announced that she visited some of the homes and the homeowners
  said they did not know about this public hearing.

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay stated that the homeowners
  were notified by certified letter.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, to postpone this until the next City Council
  Meeting. The motion died for lack of a second.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to instruct
  the Public Services Department to proceed and perform the removal of weeds in accordance
  with Sections 39568 through 39588 of the Government Code.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

OLD BUSINESS

25. Bocce Ball Survey Results

  Director of Public Services Mark Nix presented the results of staff's survey of interest for
  bocce balls courts in Mission Viejo.

City Council Minutes  7  August 18, 2014
   Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to direct staff
  to move forward with a conceptual design for bocce ball courts at a cost not to exceed
  $10,000.

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

NEW BUSINESS

City Council Minutes  8  August 18, 2014

12. Destruction of Records -- Citywide 2013 Records Purge

  This item was deferred to the next City Council Meeting.

17. Public Works Professional Services Consultant Team

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon presented the staff report.

  Council Member Schlicht expressed concern with unbalanced distribution of the non-bid
  contracts and she announced that she would present some information for the public
  record. She stated that it is good for the public to have oversight and that competition is
  crucial in bids.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to (1)
  approve the 2014-2016 Professional Services Consultant Team Roster (for plan check, design
  or other professional services); (2) authorize the City Manager to execute the first
  amendments extending the term to June 30, 2016; and (3) authorize the City Manager to
  execute contracts with Giddens Irrigation Design, Gong Enterprises, and R. Dale Hadfield,
  Landscape Architect, adding the firms to the Team.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

21. Muirlands Boulevard Street Lights (CIP 222)-Award of Construction Contract

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon presented staff report.

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: stated that we pride ourselves in being an environmentally
  conscious city and staff should have looked into solar options and spacing matters before
  proceeding with the project. He also inquired about SCE insurance and indemnity coverage
  for the electrical work that will be done.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to (1) award
  the construction contract for the subject project to Pro Tech Engineering Corporation in the
  amount of $227,127.00; and (2) authorize remittance in the amount of $180,294.50 to
  Southern California Edison (SCE) for the provision of the street light poles and fixtures and
  all wiring.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  9  August 18, 2014
   AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: requested that when the City Manager delivers his report, he comment
on the grand jury report regarding the OCFA. He also asked the City Manager to comment on the
topic of Mission Viejo liability for OCFA unfunded pensions. He further discussed his prior
questions on the Muirlands Street light project (agenda item 21.)

City Attorney’s Report

Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: asked for the statute that backs up the City Manager's opinion on SCE
insurance requirements for agenda item 21 and he recommended that the City's legal services be
put out to bid. Mr. Wontrobski noted that OCFA went out to bid for attorney services and he
questioned the City Attorney's recommendation for assistant City Attorney (agenda item 32.)

City Council Minutes  10  August 18, 2014
 32. Request for Approval of the attached Resolution Approving Mary Binning, Esq. as
  Assistant City Attorney and Reconfirming the Scope of Representation of the Office of

  City Attorney Curley presented the staff report.

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: expressed opposition to the appointment of Mary Binning as
  Assistant City Attorney. He asked where her resume is and what her specialties are.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to adopt
  Resolution 14-39 Appointing The Assistant City Attorney and Reconfirming the Scope of
  the Office of City Attorney.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury

33. Tenth Amendment to City Manager Employment Agreement

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: expressed opposition to the City Manager's proposed

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to (1) adopt

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
